title: Beacon Gateway: event hydrator, dedup & contract-timestamp aligner
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: implement a resilient, low-latency gateway (Beacon Gateway) in front of console usage event pipelines that performs event hydration (attach tenant/context), deduplication, and contract-timestamp alignment before forwarding to downstream schema validators and storage. Background: console emits high-cardinality UI and API usage events with inconsistent timestamp sources (client, server, proxy) and occasional duplicated firehose batches from browser retries. Current pipeline sees inflated counts, attribution errors across customers, and spurious schema validation noise. Goals: (1) normalize event time ordering and pick canonical event timestamp using deterministic precedence rules + clock skew heuristics; (2) eliminate duplicates with tenant-scoped idempotency windows; (3) attach derived context (user_id hash, route, feature_flags snapshot) to reduce downstream enrichment work; (4) surface soft-validation signals (probabilistic contract confidence) to allow graceful acceptance for non-breaking drift and quick operator feedback. Non-goals: full event enrichment from offline sources and long-term lineage reconciliation (handled by backfill jobs).
acceptance_criteria: Beacon Gateway accepts events and returns 2xx for valid or soft-accepted events within P95 < 100ms end-to-end
Duplicates (same tenant + event_id) are collapsed with window default 10s; dedupe rate measured and false-merge < 0.1%
Canonical timestamp selection applied according to precedence: server_received > client_sent (adjusted for skew heuristics) and recorded in canonical_timestamp field
Soft-validation mode emits contract_confidence score in event metadata; hard failures routed to quarantine topic
Canary rollout to 5% of console traffic for 72 hours with no customer-facing regressions and latency SLI degradation < 5%
Automated E2E tests and a synthetic replay harness exist covering skewed timestamps, duplicate bursts, and malformed payloads
Operational runbook and Grafana dashboard with per-tenant ingestion rate, dedupe rate, validation_reject_rate, and latency are published
notes:
Implementation will be a small stateless front proxy with sharded in-memory idempotency windows (LRU+TTL) backed by optional Redis for longer windows per-tenant. We will expose a /v1/beacon endpoint and a sidecar to forward to existing ingest topics (validated-topic / quarantine-topic). Trade-offs discussed: in-memory dedupe gives best latency but risks cold-start duplicate acceptance; Redis adds cost and operational surface area. Chosen initial mode: hybrid in-memory with Redis fallback for tenants with >200qps.

Schema validation approach: keep strict Avro/JSON schema check as downstream step; Beacon will compute a contract_confidence score using heuristics (missing optional fields, unexpected extra fields, type-coercion success). Events with confidence < 0.2 go to quarantine; 0.2-0.6 become soft-accepted with a label for downstream alerting; >0.6 are forwarded normally. This minimizes hard rejects while enabling progressive schema tightening.

Performance targets: baseline P50 30ms, P95 < 100ms at 10k events/s aggregate across all gateways. Cost estimate: additional Redis cluster (c3.medium) and CPU for lightweight hydration service.

Rollout plan: unit/integration tests -> internal traffic (synthetic) -> canary 5% (72h) -> 25% (48h) -> full. Metrics monitored at each stage with automated rollback if validation_reject_rate increases by >200% or latency SLO breach >10%.

open_questions: Should dedupe window be configurable per-customer via console (first-cut default 10s)?
Do we permit soft-accepts to be billed immediately or wait for downstream verification? (impact on invoicing accuracy)
For private/on-prem deployments, does customer want Redis included in the bundle or do they provide their own? (sales + infra contract impact)
implementation_notes:
Language: Go. Framework: internal fast-http gateway. Deployment: k8s as a deployment with HPA; sidecar pattern for forwarding. Feature flag gate (ff_beacon_gateway_enabled) per tenant. Telemetry: OpenTelemetry spans and histogram metrics. QA: synthetic replay harness under tools/ingest-replay.

Security: scrub PII before logs, enforce KMS for any persisted metadata. Security review flagged by security_review_required=true and scheduled 2026-03-05.
testing_plan: Unit tests for timestamp selection, dedupe window behavior, and confidence scoring. Integration tests against mocked validator and quarantine topic. Load test with 10k tps synthetic payloads, toggling Redis fallback. Chaos test: network partitioning between gateway and downstream to test backpressure behavior.
